title: HfO2/SiO2 high-layer-count periodic stack for maximum blocking
scientific_hypothesis: Using the full 30-layer budget with a standard periodic Bragg stack achieves superior blocking in 300-1100 nm compared to lower-layer designs, while maintaining adequate UV transmission.
design_principle: More Bragg pairs increase the stopband reflectance, improving out-of-band blocking. With 30 layers available, maximizing pair count should provide the best blocking performance while a central cavity maintains the passband.
design_variables: Individual layer thicknesses for all 21 layers (10 pairs + 1 cavity + 10 pairs)
soft_objectives: Maximize blocking depth across full out-of-band range
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count is 21, under 30-layer limit
High layer count increases deposition time and cost
HfO2 and SiO2 are conventional depositable materials
Stress accumulation across 21 layers must be managed
theory_basis: Bragg reflector stopband depth scales with pair count
expected_advantages: Maximum blocking performance within layer budget
Good margin under 30-layer limit for manufacturing tolerance
known_risks: Stress accumulation may cause delamination or cracking
May not improve UV transmission over lower-layer designs
execution_request_english: Design a high-layer-count periodic bandpass filter on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Stack: 10 periods of HfO2/SiO2 (Gao) quarter-wave pairs, one HfO2 cavity layer at center, then 10 periods of SiO2 (Gao)/HfO2 quarter-wave pairs. Total 21 layers. Optimize all individual layer thicknesses to maximize transmittance in 255-280 nm while minimizing transmittance in 300-700 nm and 700-1100 nm. No metal layers. Materials: hfo2, SiO2 (Gao).
